name: Google AlloyDB
model: PostgreSQL-compatible tables and SQL (Postgres 14 -- 18 compatibility), with pgvector-based vector search
engine_note: Postgres query engine on separate compute VMs over Google's distributed storage layer across zones; in-memory columnar engine speeds analytic scans
consistency: Postgres transaction semantics (read committed default, serializable option). Data persisted across zones; HA standby in a second zone with automatic failover. Read pools are replicas, possibly stale (docs do not say). Cross-region replication is asynchronous.
scaling: Separated storage and compute: scale the primary up, add read pool nodes for reads, cross-region secondary clusters; no automatic write sharding.
licence: Proprietary (Google Cloud managed service; AlloyDB Omni is a downloadable proprietary edition)
version_note: Latest dated change read: 2026-09-21, the columnar engine now caches HNSW vector indexes. PostgreSQL 18 compatibility went GA on 2026-03-25.
reach: Reach for it when you are on Google Cloud and want Postgres with faster analytic queries and vector search on the same operational data.
avoid: Avoid when you need to stay portable across clouds without paying for Omni, or a small database where Cloud SQL is cheaper.
escape: Adds separated storage across zones, read pools and an in-memory columnar engine for analytics over plain Postgres.
chat: Users, chats and messages plus message embeddings for search, on Google Cloud.
notes: The overview does not state whether read pool reads can lag the primary; phrased as possibly stale (they are replicas). AlloyDB Omni licence terms (free developer edition, paid production) not read in full; marked proprietary. No Jepsen analysis.
